SELECT l.lag_m, ROUND(CORR(x.v, y.v), 3) AS r, COUNT(*) AS n FROM (SELECT period, value AS v FROM because.ons_series_d7g7) x CROSS JOIN (SELECT 0 AS lag_m UNION ALL SELECT 3 AS lag_m UNION ALL SELECT 6 AS lag_m UNION ALL SELECT 9 AS lag_m UNION ALL SELECT 12 AS lag_m) l JOIN (SELECT s.period, (s.value / s.v12 - 1) * 100 AS v FROM (SELECT period, value, LAG(value, 12) OVER (ORDER BY period) AS v12, LAG(period, 12) OVER (ORDER BY period) AS p12 FROM because.fred_series_pngaseuusdm) s WHERE s.v12 IS NOT NULL AND s.v12 <> 0 AND (CAST(SUBSTR(s.period, 1, 4) AS INT) * 12 + CAST(SUBSTR(s.period, 6, 2) AS INT)) - (CAST(SUBSTR(s.p12, 1, 4) AS INT) * 12 + CAST(SUBSTR(s.p12, 6, 2) AS INT)) = 12) y ON (CAST(SUBSTR(y.period, 1, 4) AS INT) * 12 + CAST(SUBSTR(y.period, 6, 2) AS INT)) + l.lag_m = (CAST(SUBSTR(x.period, 1, 4) AS INT) * 12 + CAST(SUBSTR(x.period, 6, 2) AS INT)) WHERE SUBSTR(x.period, 1, 7) >= '2015-01' AND SUBSTR(x.period, 1, 7) <= '2022-12' GROUP BY l.lag_m ORDER BY l.lag_m

findings.statement: UK CPI annual rate (ONS D7G7): 5.4% in 2021-12 (start of 2022) -> 11.1% in 2022-10 (the 2022 peak), +5.7 pts; for context, the 2020 average was 0.8%
CPI housing, water & fuels annual rate (ONS D7GB) (level): 6.9% in 2021-12 -> 26.6% in 2022-10, a change of +19.7 pts; correlation with the target r=+0.98 at a 0-month lead
CPI food & non-alcoholic drinks annual rate (ONS D7G8) (level): 4.2% in 2021-12 -> 16.2% in 2022-10, a change of +12.0 pts; correlation with the target r=+0.93 at a 0-month lead
CPI transport annual rate (ONS D7GE) (level): 9.9% in 2021-10 -> 12.0% in 2022-08 (its best lead, 2 months earlier), a change of +2.1 pts; correlation with the target r=+0.94 at a 2-month lead
CPI services annual rate (ONS D7NN) (level): 3.4% in 2021-12 -> 6.3% in 2022-10, a change of +2.9 pts; correlation with the target r=+0.97 at a 0-month lead

European natural gas price, USD (FRED PNGASEUUSDM) (12-month % change): 122.4% in 2021-03 -> 281.9% in 2022-01 (its best lead, 9 months earlier), a change of +159.5 pts; correlation with the target r=+0.92 at a 9-month lead

Brent crude oil price, USD (FRED POILBREUSDM) (12-month % change): 110.9% in 2021-05 -> 70.9% in 2022-03 (its best lead, 7 months earlier), a change of -40.0 pts; correlation with the target r=+0.77 at a 7-month lead

Global food price index (IMF via FRED PFOODINDEXM) (12-month % change): 26.0% in 2021-03 -> 21.3% in 2022-01 (its best lead, 9 months earlier), a change of -4.7 pts; correlation with the target r=+0.82 at a 9-month lead
US dollars per pound (FRED DEXUSUK) (12-month % change): -1.0% in 2021-12 -> -17.3% in 2022-10, a change of -16.3 pts; correlation with the target r=-0.64 at a 0-month lead
UK short-term interest rate (FRED IRSTCI01GBM156N): averaged 0.18 in the 6-18 months before the 2022-10 peak (vs 0.19 in 2020); 2.19 at 2022-10
UK unemployment rate (FRED LRHUTTTTGBM156S): averaged 4.23 in the 6-18 months before the 2022-10 peak (vs 4.60 in 2020); 3.90 at 2022-10

Context (Wikipedia, 'United Kingdom cost-of-living crisis'): By January 2024, the 12-month Retail Price Index had fallen to 4% after peaking at 11.1% in October 2022, while workers' wages had risen 6.2% in the last quarter of 2023.

Context (Wikipedia, 'United Kingdom cost-of-living crisis'): Factors that have worsened the crisis since 1 April 2022 include Ofgem increasing the household energy price cap by 54%, an increase in National Insurance and a rise in Council Tax.
Context (Wikipedia, 'United Kingdom cost-of-living crisis'): In 2022, household income – whether from earnings or benefits – had not generally kept pace with rising prices.
Context (Wikipedia, 'United Kingdom cost-of-living crisis'): In April 2022, UK real wages fell by 4.5%, the sharpest fall since records began back in 2001.

Cross-source (ONS x FRED, one federated SQL JOIN on month): over 2015-01 to 2022-12, UK CPI annual rate tracks the 12-month change in European natural gas price (USD) 9 months earlier most closely (r = 0.90, n = 96 months, strong); same-month r = 0.45

answer.summary: UK inflation rose in 2022: 5.4% (2021-12) -> 11.1% (2022-10 peak), +5.7 pts; 2020 average 0.8%. The evidence is consistent with these drivers: (1) household energy inflation (CPI housing, water & fuels) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak; (2) food inflation (CPI food & non-alcoholic drinks) rose during the run-up to the 2022 peak; (3) the 12-month change in the pound's value against the dollar fell during the run-up to the 2022 peak.
